results.content: Nevertheless, there has been a lack of embedding methods that can guarantee (i) embedding the dynamical system comprehensively, including the vector fields (ODE form) of the dynamics, and (ii) preserving the consistency of control effect between the original and latent space. To address these challenges, we propose Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control (KEEC) to learn an embedding of the states and vector fields such that a Koopman operator is approximated as the latent dynamics. In this paper, we aim to find an isometric and equivariant mapping such that the flows and vector fields of the original nonlinear dynamics are comprehensively mapped to a latent controllable system, thus preserving the control effect in both the original and latent spaces. We learn an isometric and equivariant function to embed the control dynamics into a latent space such that the latent dynamics can be represented by a Koopman operator. Besides, due to the assumption of control-affine systems, the embedded system dynamics actuation part () provides the information of vector fields to derive an analytical form of policy extraction, i.e. representing greedy policy with value function (see Section 3.4). ‣ 3.4 Optimal Control on Equivariant Vector Field ‣ 3 Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control ‣ Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control") demonstrates that we can solve the control problems based on the latent value function without mapping back to the original space. ‣ 3.4 Optimal Control on Equivariant Vector Field ‣ 3 Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control ‣ Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control"), the optimal policy for the value function in the latent space has an analytical solution:. ‣ 3.4 Optimal Control on Equivariant Vector Field ‣ 3 Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control ‣ Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control") holds, the approximated latent value function will point-wisely converge to the optimal , and the convergence rate is quadratic as follows:. ‣ 3.4 Optimal Control on Equivariant Vector Field ‣ 3 Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control ‣ Koopman Embedded Equivariant Control"), if the value function has a quadratic form, i.e., with being symmetric positive definite matrix, being a constant, then, the optimal action is:.

Stack Exchange network consists of 183 Q&A communities including Stack Overflow, the largest, most trusted online community for developers to learn, share their knowledge, and build their careers. # [$E[X\_t-X\_{t+1}|F\_t]=[X\_t-X\_{t+1}|X\_0,...,X\_t]?$ [closed]](/questions/4526662/ex-t-x-t1f-t-x-t-x-t1x-0-x-t). What I want to confirm is the $F\_t$ has nothing different with the history of the stochastic process. Let $\left\{X\_t\right\}\_t$ be a stochastic process, $F\_t$ be the natural filtration. **My question:** Is this equation correct $$E[X\_t-X\_{t+1}|F\_t]=[X\_t-X\_{t+1}|X\_0,...,X\_t]?$$. asked Sep 7, 2022 at 14:11. 18333 silver badges1111 bronze badges. ## 1 Answer 1. Yes, the natural filtration is just the history of the process. What you wrote is correct when $\{F\_t\}\_t$ is the natural filtration of $\{X\_t\}\_t$ (assuming you're working in discrete time, where it makes sense to write $X\_0,X\_1,...,X\_t$). However, the natural filtration might not be the only filtration you are interested in. Suppose that $\{F\_t\}\_t$ is still the natural filtration of $\{X\_t\}\_t$ and define $Y\_t := X\_t^2$. Then \begin{align\*} E[Y\_t-Y\_{t+1}|F\_t] = E[Y\_t-Y\_{t+1}|X\_0,...,X\_t], \end{align\*} which is not always the same as $E[Y\_t-Y\_{t+1}|Y\_0,...,Y\_t]$, because $F\_t$ is the natural filtration of $X\_t$ instead of the natural filtration of $Y\_t$. $Y\_t$ doesn't tell you anything about the sign of $X\_t$, so those filtrations are not the same when $X\_t$ can take on positive or negative values. answered Sep 7, 2022 at 16:41. 14.2k11 gold badge1616 silver badges3030 bronze badges. results.title: The Drift Engine: Predicting When and Where Transformers Will Forget | by Satyam Mishra | Medium
results.content: # The Drift Engine: Predicting When and Where Transformers Will Forget. ## Modeling Semantic Drift with Koopman Operators and Entropy Fields. Modern language models like GPT-4 are brilliant predictors. But there’s something they consistently fail at over long sequences: **remembering what they just meant**. It’s **semantic drift:** a measurable degradation in meaning coherence as generation continues. This blog introduces a **novel, predictive, and mathematical framework** to model and forecast this phenomenon using **Koopman operator theory**, **semantic entropy**, and **spectral dynamics**. > ***The Drift Engine:*** *A Koopman Spectral System for Forecasting Transformer Forgetting.*. > ***Semantic Drift*** *is the progressive deviation in the meaning representation of tokens in a generated sequence, such that the later tokens become statistically* ***less reversible*** *to their source context.*. They generate token x\_t​ based on past tokens x\_semantic irreversibility. We model this using a **reversibility function** R(x\_t,x\_. We propose modeling the **semantic evolution of a token sequence** as a **nonlinear dynamical system**:. Instead of learning f directly, we **lift** this system to a linear regime using a **Koopman operator** K:. To quantify drift, we define **semantic entropy** over the latent space:. Low-entropy = focused, clear meaning. We analyze eigen-decomposition of the Koopman operator:. Each eigenvector/mode shows how **a semantic feature changes** over time. Predicting the Onset of Forgetting. We define a **semantic forgetting detector**:. If v\_drift > ϵ and ∇H\_t > δ, raise a drift alert. Entropy is estimated by KDE (Kernel Density Estimation) in semantic space. for each sequence x_1, ..., x_T: embed = BERT(x_t) phi = nonlinear_lift(embed) koopman = least_squares(phi[:-1], phi[1:]) entropy = estimate_entropy(phi) drift = norm(phi[t+1] - phi[t]) if drift > threshold and entropy_grad > delta: alert("Forgetting detected"). Satyam’s Explanation for Kids. Imagine a robot writing a story with you. After some time, it starts saying silly things or forgets the plot. Our method tells the robot:. You’re drifting too far, come back before it’s too late!”*. It’s like giving the robot a **map and a compass** so it doesn’t get lost while telling stories. This post was originally written on Substack:. `#AIresearch, #SemanticDrift, #Transformers, #KoopmanOperator, #Entropy, #Forecasting, #DeepLearning, #LLMs, #DynamicalSystems, #NLP, #satmis`. ## Written by Satyam Mishra.
